# We are now Cencora. Our shared identity unites us.

Cencora brings the companies and services of AmerisourceBergen together under one new name.

[ Meet Cencora ][86]
[A banner that says We Are Cencora on a pink and purple background]

# Marketplace gives pharmacies access to thousands of uniquely curated front-of-store products

We’re reimagining the procurement process by enabling pharmacies to source all the products they
need from front to back through one convenient platform.
[ Learn more ][87]
[A person viewing the Marketplace homepage on their laptop]

## We are united in our responsibility
## to create healthier futures.

As we pursue our purpose, we make a positive impact on the health of people and animals around the
world.

### Pharmaceutical distribution solutions

Our wholesale and specialty distribution services ensure that crucial medications efficiently,
reliably and securely reach their destinations every day.
[ Learn more ][88]
[AB_1Card_03]

### Manufacturer solutions

In addition to distribution and logistics, we help pharmaceutical manufacturers bring their products
to market – and assist with each step from pre-commercial and clinical trial to broad market
availability and patient adherence.
[ Learn more ][89]
[AB_2_3_Card_03]

### Provider solutions

Our solutions power patient care for pharmacies, physician practices, hospitals and health systems.
[ Learn more ][90]
[AB_2_3_Card_05]

### Animal health solutions

We deliver distribution, technology and innovation for veterinarians, livestock producers and
manufacturers to make a meaningful difference in their businesses and the health of animals.
[ Learn more ][91]
[GettyImages-907614352_JPG]

## In the news

Read the latest press releases and media mentions.
[ Explore newsroom ][92]

## Insights

Access the newest in thought leadership.
[ Explore insights ][93]

# Careers with purpose

With a global presence and 44,000+ team members strong, AmerisourceBergen is committed to making a
difference in the future of health.
[ Explore careers ][94]
[GettyImages-1178

# Building a world of health around every individual

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

## Combining our strengths for you

Health services Health insurance Pharmacy Prescription drug coverage

### Health services

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

[Explore our services ][110]

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

[Discover Aetna plans ][111]

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

### Prescription drug coverage

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

[Learn about drug coverage ][113]

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

 

## Tricia Fitzgerald's Story

Meet the Fitzgerald family: Mom, dad, and 6 kids. Life with chronic conditions is not simple, but
with CVS Health by their side, managing chronic conditions becomes a little… simpler.

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

## Combining our strengths for you

Health services Health insurance Pharmacy Prescription drug coverage

### Health services

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

[Explore our services ][110]

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

[Discover Aetna plans ][111]

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

### Prescription drug coverage

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

[Learn about drug coverage ][113]

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

# With the Patient at the Heart

We develop software that helps people get well, helps people stay well, and helps future generations
be healthier.
[Our story →][1]

## Nurses Save Time and Keep Families Connected Using AI

At UNC Health, Riverside Health, and WakeMed, nurses reduce documentation time and improve patient &
family communication with the help of Art, Epic’s AI for clinicians.
[Learn more →][2]

## Teamwork Staff Scheduling Delivers Faster Care Coordination and Reduces Administrative Work at
## Health Systems Worldwide

Organizations report on the benefits of Teamwork—the first application in EpicOps, Epic’s integrated
Enterprise Resource Planning suite built for healthcare.
[Learn more →][3]

## UnityPoint Health Saves Lives with Better Sepsis Detection and Treatment in Pregnancy

Detection criteria and care path built into Epic EHR help clinicians identify sepsis in maternal
patients sooner and reduce time to treatment.
[Learn more →][4]

Alongside healthcare providers, Epic is taking legal action to defend patient privacy.
[Read more →][5]

# Our Software

Our software makes it possible for every patient to have a single, comprehensive medical record that
informs and is informed by their health experiences. The goal is higher-quality, more personalized
care that's simpler for patients, medical professionals, and everyone who makes healthcare happen.
[Learn more about our software →][6]

### From Phone Tag to Push Notifications: How Four Health Systems Closed the Loop on Critical Lab
### Communication

July 06, 2026
Four health systems are among those that have replaced phone calls for critical lab result
communication with Epic push notifications, achieving acknowledgement times under one
minute—compared to an average of seven to twelve minutes previously. Lab staff save approximately
ten minutes per result, which adds up to enough time saved at one organization for 15 full-time
staff members to focus on higher-value work. Clinicians acted faster on critical results, where
every minute matters.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][8]
[Providing Pain Relief for Sickle Cell Crises Faster with Personal, Portable Care Plans]

### Providing Pain Relief for Sickle Cell Crises Faster with Personal, Portable Care Plans

June 22, 2026
Manchester University NHS Foundation Trust developed a digital sickle cell care program to improve
tracking and transparency of emergency pain management. The program includes personalized emergency
care plans and an ED order set. Patients went from having no digital care plans to 89% coverage, and
active patient portal usage among people with sickle cell disease increased from 43% to 58%.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][9]
[Using Telecritical Care to Reduce ICU Mortality]

### Using Telecritical Care to Reduce ICU Mortality

June 15, 2026
To provide expert overnight critical care, Kaiser Permanente Northern California implemented a
telecritical care program that connects remote intensivists and nurses to ICUs through real-time
monitoring, camera feeds, and instant communication. Today, the program is in use across 18 ICUs and
is associated with a 7% reduction in adjusted mortality.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][10]
[AI Coding Assistant Reduces Chart Review Time by 20%, Freeing Coders for Higher-Value Work]

### AI Coding Assistant Reduces Chart Review Time by 20%, Freeing Coders for Higher-Value Work

June 08, 2026
After implementing Epic’s AI Professional Billing Coding Assistant, coders at Baptist Health in
Jacksonville, Florida spend 20% less time reviewing charts—an estimated $924,000 in annual labor
savings. Clean claim rates and coder productivity have also improved.
[Read the full story on EpicShare →][11]

    provide lower-cost options for prescription medications and therapies.

    We help to ensure the financial wellbeing of pharmacies and health systems and support a stable
    work environment for their employees.

# Advancing Health Outcomes for All®

[ Discover McKesson ][125]

## Making Healthcare Happen

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Business Solutions
 

## Our Areas of Focus

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

[ Learn More ][126]

setting.]

Strengthening Healthcare
 

## Powering Care Locally

For nearly two centuries, McKesson has strengthened the systems that move care forward by supporting
providers, enabling access to medicines and therapies, and removing barriers across the patient
journey.

# Advancing Health Outcomes for All®

[ Discover McKesson ][125]

## Making Healthcare Happen

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Business Solutions
 

## Our Areas of Focus

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

For nearly two centuries, McKesson has strengthened the systems that move care forward by supporting

### Join us and change the world of medicine

Life at Moderna

][41]

## So, what is mRNA?

Messenger RNA (mRNA) already exists in your body. It carries a “message”–instructions that direct
your cells what to do.

Fighting disease differentlyLimitless treatmentsHelping more peopleMore medicines, faster
[Macro shot of hand skin texture][Macro shot of hand skin texture]

### Fighting disease differently

mRNA medicines fight diseases in a different way than traditional medicine by prompting your immune
system to create the tools to treat or prevent disease.

[
Learn more about mRNA
][42]
[Man looking at slide and smiling][Man looking at slide and smiling]

### Limitless treatments

We believe that if mRNA can treat one disease, it can treat many diseases. We will use mRNA to treat
diseases for which there are currently no treatments.

[
Learn more about mRNA
][43]
[Older couple sitting at table and smiling][Older couple sitting at table and smiling]

### Helping more people

mRNA medicine contains no animal products or preservatives, making medicine accessible for as many
people as possible.

[
Learn more about mRNA
][44]
[Close up of scientific equipment][Close up of scientific equipment]

### More medicines, faster

Our platform enables rapid design, research and testing of multiple mRNAs, within days. Our novel
production methods allow us to get medicines to more people, faster.

[
Learn more about mRNA
][45]

#### Revolutionary medicines enable us to enrich and extend life for people living with all types of
#### diseases. 

[Internal medicine graphical thumbnail portrait image 2]

##### [ Internal Medicine ][109]

[ View All Internal Medicine ][110]

We’re developing therapies to treat, slow, or prevent disease progression and improve the quality of
life for patients with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular and kidney diseases. 

[Inflammation and Immunology graphical thumbnail portrait image 3]

##### [ Inflammation & Immunology ][111]

[ View All Inflammation & Immunology ][112]

We look for treatments that provide more than just symptom relief, in order to address the root
cause of chronic inflammatory diseases at a molecular level

[Vaccine graphical thumbnail portrait image 4]

##### [ Vaccines ][113]

[ View All Vaccines ][114]

Vaccines are the single most important innovation in the science of health to significantly reduce
the threat of diseases that were once widespread and oftentimes fatal. 

[Vaccines][115] 
[Milestones][116] 
[Pipeline & Clinical Trials ][117]

[Oncology graphical thumbnail portrait image 5]

##### [ Oncology ][118]

[ View All Oncology ][119]

Cancer treatment needs to be transformed across the entire landscape to significantly improve the
lives of cancer patients worldwide.

[Oncology][120]

# Celebrating America’s 250th Anniversary

Founded in Brooklyn in 1849, Pfizer has channeled American ambition into generations of
breakthroughs that change patients' lives.

 

[Our History][90]

[Photograph of a woman smiling as a child lifts a toy plane toward the sky.]

#### Pfizer's 2025 Impact Report

Every year, we take stock of the impact our work has on the world, the environment, and people
themselves.

[Read the report][91]

### Products

Every product is the result of 1,500 scientists overseeing more than 500,000 lab tests and over 36
clinical trials before the first prescription.

Pfizer RxPathways connects eligible patients to a range of assistance programs that offer insurance
support, co-pay help, and medicines for free or at a savings.

Areas of Focus

#### Revolutionary medicines enable us to enrich and extend life for people living with all types of
#### diseases. 

[Internal medicine graphical thumbnail portrait image 2]

##### [ Internal Medicine ][109]

[ View All Internal Medicine ][110]

We’re developing therapies to treat, slow, or prevent disease progression and improve the quality of
life for patients with obesity, type 2 diabetes, and cardiovascular and kidney diseases. 

[Inflammation and Immunology graphical thumbnail portrait image 3]

##### [ Inflammation & Immunology ][111]

[ View All Inflammation & Immunology ][112]

We look for treatments that provide more than just symptom relief, in order to address the root
cause of chronic inflammatory diseases at a molecular level

[Vaccine graphical thumbnail portrait image 4]

##### [ Vaccines ][113]

[ View All Vaccines ][114]

Vaccines are the single most important innovation in the science of health to significantly reduce
the threat of diseases that were once widespread and oftentimes fatal. 

[Vaccines][115] 
[Milestones][116]

##### [ Oncology ][118]

[ View All Oncology ][119]

Cancer treatment needs to be transformed across the entire landscape to significantly improve the
lives of cancer patients worldwide.

[Oncology][120]

## About

#### Starting with Charles Pfizer inventing an almond-flavored antiparasite medicine in 1849, our
#### people have always been innovators and trailblazers, committed to finding the next cure. 

[ Learn More About Us Details][124]

#### An Accord for a Healthier World

Where people live shouldn’t impact the quality of their healthcare and income shouldn’t determine
health outcomes.

HDR HD Dual Lens Camera Module

The HDR HD Dual‑Lens Camera Module combines a high‑performance 2 MP sensor with a complementary 1.3
MP sensor and advanced NIR technology to deliver clear, dynamic-range‑optimized imaging. Its
dual‑lens stereo configuration supports depth sensing—making it ideal for face recognition systems
requiring both accuracy and anti‑spoofing (liveness detection). Compliant with the USB Video Class
standard, this camera module offers true plug‑and‑play functionality—no drivers, no hassle.

Designed for integration into a variety of systems—from entrance‑control terminals to interactive
advertising displays—its compact, industrial‑grade build ensures reliability in continuous‑operation
environments. With broad operating system compatibility (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android), it
seamlessly adapts to your existing hardware and software ecosystem.

## **
## **

## **Key Features**
* 2 MP + 1.3 MP Full-HD CMOS Sensors
  One 2 megapixel and one 1.3 megapixel sensor deliver crisp 1920×1080 and 1280×960 video at up to
  30 fps, ensuring detailed imaging and flexible deployment for recognition and surveillance.
* High Dynamic Range (HDR)
  Advanced HDR processing balances exposure across shadows and highlights—ideal for challenging
  lighting in access control, advertising kiosks, or smart ATMs.
* Dual‑Lens Stereo Vision
  Two aligned lenses provide depth perception for accurate liveness detection, 3D mapping, and
  improved recognition reliability.
* UVC‑Compliant, Driver‑Free
  Fully USB Video Class (UVC) compliant—no custom driver installation required. Simply plug into any
  UVC‑capable host (Windows, Linux, Mac, Android) and begin streaming.
* Plug‑and‑Play Connectivity
  Standard USB 2.0 interface; bus‑powered design eliminates the need for external adapters.
* Wide Application Scope
  Perfect for security monitoring, biometric access control, data collection, smart terminals,
  advertising machines, teleconferencing, and robotics.
* Compact, Industrial‑Grade Housing
  Robust black metal enclosure with M12‑mountable lenses, suitable for harsh environments and
  prolonged operation.

Shenzhen Ruishi Technology Co., Ltd. is a high-tech enterprise specializing in camera module
development and production. With a registered capital of 12 million RMB and over 110 employees, it
boasts an R&D center and production workshop in Shenzhen, holding ISO9001 and ISO14001
certifications.

WELCOME TO OUR FACTORY!

Ruishi specializes in manufacturing camera modules, leading visual programs for a smarter future. We

HDR HD Dual Lens Camera Module

The HDR HD Dual‑Lens Camera Module combines a high‑performance 2 MP sensor with a complementary 1.3
MP sensor and advanced NIR technology to deliver clear, dynamic-range‑optimized imaging. Its
dual‑lens stereo configuration supports depth sensing—making it ideal for face recognition systems
requiring both accuracy and anti‑spoofing (liveness detection). Compliant with the USB Video Class
standard, this camera module offers true plug‑and‑play functionality—no drivers, no hassle.

Designed for integration into a variety of systems—from entrance‑control terminals to interactive
advertising displays—its compact, industrial‑grade build ensures reliability in continuous‑operation
environments. With broad operating system compatibility (Windows, Linux, macOS, Android), it
seamlessly adapts to your existing hardware and software ecosystem.

## **
## **

## **Key Features**
* 2 MP + 1.3 MP Full-HD CMOS Sensors
  One 2 megapixel and one 1.3 megapixel sensor deliver crisp 1920×1080 and 1280×960 video at up to
  30 fps, ensuring detailed imaging and flexible deployment for recognition and surveillance.
* High Dynamic Range (HDR)
  Advanced HDR processing balances exposure across shadows and highlights—ideal for challenging
  lighting in access control, advertising kiosks, or smart ATMs.
* Dual‑Lens Stereo Vision
  Two aligned lenses provide depth perception for accurate liveness detection, 3D mapping, and
  improved recognition reliability.
* UVC‑Compliant, Driver‑Free
  Fully USB Video Class (UVC) compliant—no custom driver installation required. Simply plug into any
  UVC‑capable host (Windows, Linux, Mac, Android) and begin streaming.
* Plug‑and‑Play Connectivity
  Standard USB 2.0 interface; bus‑powered design eliminates the need for external adapters.
* Wide Application Scope
  Perfect for security monitoring, biometric access control, data collection, smart terminals,
  advertising machines, teleconferencing, and robotics.
* Compact, Industrial‑Grade Housing
  Robust black metal enclosure with M12‑mountable lenses, suitable for harsh environments and
  prolonged operation.

## 

[HDR HD Dual Lens Camera Module]

## About Us

Shenzhen Ruishi Technology Co., Ltd. is a high-tech enterprise specializing in camera module
development and production. With a registered capital of 12 million RMB and over 110 employees, it
boasts an R&D center and production workshop in Shenzhen, holding ISO9001 and ISO14001
certifications.

## Les 15 ans de l'Autorité de la concurrence

L’Autorité fêtait ses 15 ans le 5 novembre 2024, dans le cadre d’un événement placé sous le haut
patronage du Président de la République.

[
[eco]
][81]

## Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN)

Créé en mai 2004, le Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN) fête cette année son 20ème anniversaire.
Entre mai 2004 et décembre 2023, les autorités nationales de concurrence ont rendu plus de 1 700
décisions fondées sur l'article 101 et/ou l'article 102. Les autorités nationales de concurrence ont
lancé en moyenne 140 enquêtes et adopté 75 décisions chaque année.

[
[podcast ]
][82]

## Cartels & Cie

Cartels & Cie est un podcast dédié aux grandes affaires démantelées par l'Autorité, qui se propose
d'emmener l'auditeur dans les coulisses de ses enquêtes, au cœur de scandales économiques impliquant
des entreprises mondiales.

[
[Guide PME]
][83]

## Espace PME

Dans une démarche de pédagogie, l’Autorité a créé un espace en ligne, intégralement dédié aux PME.
Un guide est mis à leur disposition afin qu'elles connaissent mieux les règles et puissent faire
valoir leurs droits.

Des questions sur vos démarches, des procédures en cours... Contactez-nous !

## Les 15 ans de l'Autorité de la concurrence

L’Autorité fêtait ses 15 ans le 5 novembre 2024, dans le cadre d’un événement placé sous le haut
patronage du Président de la République.

[
[eco]

## Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN)

Créé en mai 2004, le Réseau européen de concurrence (ECN) fête cette année son 20ème anniversaire.
Entre mai 2004 et décembre 2023, les autorités nationales de concurrence ont rendu plus de 1 700
décisions fondées sur l'article 101 et/ou l'article 102. Les autorités nationales de concurrence ont
lancé en moyenne 140 enquêtes et adopté 75 décisions chaque année.

[podcast ]

## Cartels & Cie

Cartels & Cie est un podcast dédié aux grandes affaires démantelées par l'Autorité, qui se propose
d'emmener l'auditeur dans les coulisses de ses enquêtes, au cœur de scandales économiques impliquant
des entreprises mondiales.

## Espace PME

Dans une démarche de pédagogie, l’Autorité a créé un espace en ligne, intégralement dédié aux PME.
Un guide est mis à leur disposition afin qu'elles connaissent mieux les règles et puissent faire
valoir leurs droits.

# e7 Health

[Vaccine Services]

## We are now e7 Health!

Why e7 Health? Due to our success and growth, we wanted a name that would more adequately represent
the 7 areas of health care (Travel Medicine, Student Health, Corporate Health Services, Drug
Testing, STD Testing, Physicals and Labs, and Vaccines) offerings we provide and to highlight
advanced technology that we are using to integrate all 7 areas of health care.

## A Preventative Health and Wellness Company

e7 Health is a preventative health and wellness company that is supervised by Board Certified
Doctors. We offer same day and next day appointments and allow you to book your appointments online!
We specialize in travel medicine, student health, employee health, drug testing, STD testing,
physical exams, immigration exams, and laboratory services. We are committed to providing the safest
and highest quality care to our patients and clients. We are proud of the highly qualified and
dedicated professional staff at e7 Health for their commitment to providing a positive and
comfortable clinic for our patients. We strive every day to ensure that all of our patients are
satisfied and well taken care of. We look forward to serving you!

the 7 areas of health care (Travel Medicine, Student Health, Corporate Health Services, Drug
Testing, STD Testing, Physicals and Labs, and Vaccines) offerings we provide and to highlight
advanced technology that we are using to integrate all 7 areas of health care.

## A Preventative Health and Wellness Company

e7 Health is a preventative health and wellness company that is supervised by Board Certified
Doctors. We offer same day and next day appointments and allow you to book your appointments online!

physical exams, immigration exams, and laboratory services. We are committed to providing the safest

dedicated professional staff at e7 Health for their commitment to providing a positive and
comfortable clinic for our patients. We strive every day to ensure that all of our patients are
satisfied and well taken care of. We look forward to serving you!

# See what your competitors

While others chase press releases and earnings calls, we capture real intelligence from the data
trails companies leave behind unknowingly — whether competitors, acquisition targets, potential
partners, or emerging disruptors.

Book a Demo

## Trusted by teams at

[Intuit][S2A][Eleventh Hour Group][Abridge]
The Problem

## Why traditional intelligence falls short
* Curated narrativePress releases, earnings calls, official announcements — that's the story
  companies want you to see. By the time something is announced, it's too late to respond
  strategically. You're reacting, not planning.

  else uses. If you're reading it, so are your competitors.
* Data without contextTraditional tools bombard you with notifications — a job posting here, a doc
  update there. You spend hours trying to figure out what matters. You have alerts, not answers.

][13]

# FAQs

Common questions from organizations adopting HASH. Don't see yours here? [Get in touch][14].

What is HASH?

HASH is an open-source platform that turns your organization's raw information — across databases,
applications, fileshares, sensor feeds, chats, and more — into a continuously-updated **world
model**: a knowledge graph of the entities and relationships you care about, paired with a process
graph of the workflows they participate in.

From that one model you can run analytics, simulate what-if scenarios, automate workflows, ground AI
agents in real operational context, and govern access at fine granularity. In effect, HASH does the
job that a data warehouse, semantic layer, process modeler, governance suite, and AI integration
platform would otherwise each do separately — in one place. The other questions on this page expand
on specific aspects of that.

What kinds of things can HASH help with?

At a very high level, HASH helps you do four kinds of work in one place: integrate data from across
the systems your organization already uses, automate workflows and decisions that depend on it,
simulate how those workflows behave under different conditions, and govern the resulting model
end-to-end — who has access, where data came from, and how it has changed over time.

In practice that translates into things like steering and monitoring supply chains, running risk and
exposure models in regulated industries, building internal operational dashboards and tools,
modeling research hypotheses, grounding AI agents in real organizational context so they can act
safely, and replacing what would otherwise be a piecemeal collection of point tools (catalog,
governance, MDM, semantic layer, workflow automation, simulation) with **one coherent platform**.
HASH is domain-agnostic — the same building blocks that an industrial team uses for inventory
tracking are the ones a research team uses to model experiments, or a finance team uses to manage
exposure limits.

Does HASH require an existing data warehouse or lake?

HASH is designed to be useful from day one, regardless of the maturity of your existing data
infrastructure. Many organizations adopt HASH precisely because they want to **start organizing and
governing their information** — and you don't need a pre-existing warehouse, lake, or ETL pipeline
to begin.

HASH can serve as your source of truth from the outset, or sit alongside whatever systems you
already have, growing with your data practice over time.

Is HASH a replacement for traditional data warehouses and lakes?

HASH can fully replace a traditional warehouse or lake — many customers adopt HASH as their primary
semantic data backbone and retire (or shrink) their legacy stores over time — or it can sit
**alongside what you already have**, ingesting from your warehouse or lake as a source while

#### Detailed Market Analysis

The pharmaceutical industry is undergoing a remarkable digital transformation, supported by concrete
market research and verified statistics. The scale of this transformation is evidenced by the
pharmaceutical digital platform market’s projected growth from $4.92 billion in 2023 to $34.12
billion by 2032, representing a robust CAGR of 24.35%. This growth is driven by widespread cloud
adoption, with approximately 80% of pharmaceutical companies already utilizing cloud computing
solutions and 95% expected to be fully cloud-operational within two years.

The transformation is happening across multiple dimensions, with web-based solutions dominating at
72.27% market share and AI-driven engagement representing 27.05% of patient engagement solutions.
Quality management systems are also evolving, with the market expected to grow from $1.87 billion in
2024 to $3.85 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of 12.99%. This digital evolution is particularly strong in
North America, which holds a 43.6% share in patient engagement solutions and 39% of the quality
management software market. Implementation timelines vary by solution complexity, ranging from 3-6
months for modular SaaS deployments to 9-18 months for full-suite implementations, reflecting the
industry’s methodical approach to digital adoption while maintaining compliance with regulatory
requirements.

## Navagen Products.

Navagen Products, a private company with head office in Bangalore, was incorporated in March 2011.
The company is specialized in the production of affordable and economical packaging solution for the
transport and distribution of temperature sensitive products such as pharmaceutical, healthcare,
food products and perishable commodities like fruits, vegetables, flowers etc.

## Welcome to NCCVMRC

During the various past State Expanded Programme Immunization Officers/Cold Chain Officers Review
meeting request has been made by the State Cold Chain Officers to have a system which will be
helpful in managing and monitoring the cold chain equipment and also helpful in taking management
decisions related to cold chain using real time information, similar to how structured digital tools
like a [Remarkable Planner][13] help organize tasks, records, and daily workflows. Action on the
felt need of MIS system the MoHFW in partnership with UNICEF developed the web based NCCMIS to
monitor the cold chain system real time setting across the country.

It is envisaged as a tool for planning and taking management decision based on real time
information, as a monitoring tool for current equipment status, as a repository of cold chain
equipment for the country and as a platform for future innovations in cold chain and vaccine
management. In the same way, platforms like [casino Belgie online][14] demonstrate how digital
ecosystems can centralize data and streamline user decisions.

The MoHFW looks at NCCMIS not only as a software but as a comprehensive tool to streamline the cold
chain system. It is envisaged as a tool for planning and taking management decision based on real
time information, as a monitoring tool for current equipment status, as a repository of cold chain
equipment for the country and as a platform for future innovations in cold chain and vaccine
management.

NIHFW, through the NCCVMRC, is responsible for the overall maintenance and implementation monitoring
of NCCMIS across the country including providing helping support to end users.

Maintaining balanced energy levels doesn’t have to be complicated. [the official ArthroNeo24
platform][16], you can take a simple, consistent approach to wellness — focusing on steady glucose
levels, better focus, and long-term vitality.

Professional [Hair restoration surgery in Istanbul][17] at LookMedic offers specialized solutions
for both men and women facing various stages of hair loss. We address conditions ranging from
receding temple hairlines to traction alopecia using surgeon-led procedures. To maximize patient
comfort, we offer needle-free anesthesia and sedation options, ensuring a painless experience. Our
medical team employs precise graft planning for perfect symmetry and density. Whether you require a
high-graft Sapphire FUE session or a no-shave DHI procedure, our focus remains on delivering results
that blend seamlessly with your natural hair.

## **Testimonials**

I am pleased to share my positive experience with Archivos de Ciencia e Investigación (ADCI). The
editorial team is highly professional and exceptionally prompt in their communication, ensuring a
smooth and efficient publication process. Uploading the manuscript was straightforward, with clear
instructions and an intuitive submission platform. The follow-up steps were equally well-guided and
user-friendly, making the entire process hassle-free. I truly appreciate the journal’s commitment to
supporting authors and maintaining high editorial standards.

**Sandhya Ahuja**

The author received an honorary PhD in mathematics and majored in engineering at MIT. His approach
is “quantitative and precision medicine”. He was thankful to publish his major articles in OPAST
group. He also recommended your journals to his colleagues. He strongly supports a friendly
connection with the author as a person as well.

**GERALD C. HSU**
EclaireMD Foundation, USA

All thanks and appreciation to you. I will communicate with my colleagues looking for your
distinguished magazine. I loved having my paper published in your esteemed journal.

**Azab Alaziz Al Hashimi**
Direction of Information Management and Information Security, International Arbitrator and Writer,
Switzerland

I am glad to have my papers reviewed by the Journal of Opast Publications. Editorial Board Members
understanding and flexibility of reviewing is appreciable

**Berov G. Lyubomir**
Engineer, Independent Innovative Ideas Researcher, Bulgaria

Advance in Environmental Waste Management & Recycling is a new international journal, full of
interesting & novel topics, ideas & information. It is characterized by extremely fast turnaround
times (less than 4 weeks!) for articles that are of interest to the editorial board. I heartily
recommend this journal for scientists in "publish or perish mode" for whom priority of publication
is of paramount importance.

**Paul Alexander Comet**
Consultant, Houston, USA

I thank your journal and you for publishing our research which has attracted a bigger audience
within a short period of time. Of course, your journal and you, the editor rendered an excellent
service to us, as authors. I appreciate very much the process of your journal that has given value
for our time and work. I hope to contact you soon for the next research article.

**Shantha Indrajith Hikkaduwa Liyanage**
Senior Lecturer Faculty of Business and Accountancy, Botho University, Gaborone, Botswana

There are no words to describe my gratitude to your journal (Opast group). Being Kansas based, the
state of Superman, you are my heroes!!! It is the first time for me to be in a truthful, honest, and
productive scientific relationship. My experience so far with you has shown me that I belong to a
very promising, productive, aspiring, and energetic professional team. But most of all, I have to
say that the journal, besides the dissemination of science, strongly supports a friendly connection
with the author as a person as well. I consider myself honored to be a part of this scientific
family.

**Alexandros Senarelis-Sinaris**
Author in Clinical-Experimental Immunology & Research US

I am glad to have to publish my research article in your journal. I would recommend to my colleagues
to join in OPAST Membership category

**DELIATERE SASPONZA**
Dokuz Eylül University, Engineering Faculty, Environmental Engineering Department Buca-İzmir,
Kaynaklar Campus, Turkey

A study entitled "Why are diabetic patients still having hyperglycemia despite the use of diet
regulation, anti glycemic medication, and insulin?" was published by the International Journal of
Diabetes & Metabolic Disorders and it was very successful because I could disseminate my ideas in
the whole world using this publication and I am still using this publication in many conferences
worldwide. I thank you very much to the directors and editors of this journal to help me in this
work and divulgation of this other reasoning regarding diabetes diagnoses and treatment.

**Huang Wei Ling**
Infectious Disease Specialist (ID Specialist), General Practitioner, Nutrition Doctor,
Acupuncturist, Pain Management, Medical Acupuncture, and Pain Management Clinic, Franca, Sao Paulo,
Brazil

It was great publishing my research article in this journal as I got exposed not only in my country
but throughout the world. The Editors and Editorial Board have precisely gone through the article
and hence I am thankful to them.

**Khalid Aljabri**
Consultant

## 1. Understanding the Role of Pharma Regulatory Affairs

Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs is a multidisciplinary function within the pharmaceutical and
biotechnology industries. It plays a critical role in ensuring that all products—drugs, biologics,

## 1. Understanding the Role of Pharma Regulatory Affairs

Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs is a multidisciplinary function within the pharmaceutical and
biotechnology industries. It plays a critical role in ensuring that all products—drugs, biologics,
and medical devices—comply with the regulations and standards required by regulatory agencies across
various countries. The regulatory affairs department acts as the interface between pharmaceutical
companies and regulatory bodies such as the FDA (United States), EMA (European Union), CDSCO

approving drug applications, overseeing safety reporting, and enforcing post-approval compliance.

At its core, regulatory affairs involves the preparation, compilation, and submission of a wide
range of regulatory documents. These documents include dossiers (CTD/eCTD), product labels, periodic
safety reports, clinical trial applications, and responses to regulatory queries. In addition, the
regulatory team ensures that the company’s products are registered correctly in each market,
labeling is compliant, and pharmacovigilance systems are in place. Regulatory professionals must
stay up to date with evolving legislation and guidance documents, as non-compliance can result in
delayed product approvals, fines, or even market bans.

The scope of regulatory affairs is not limited to product approval. It extends to lifecycle
management, including post-marketing surveillance, renewals, and variations. Companies often rely on
regulatory intelligence to anticipate changes in global legislation and proactively adjust their
strategies. As global markets expand, pharmaceutical companies increasingly need to harmonize their
regulatory strategies across jurisdictions while addressing country-specific requirements. This need
gives rise to regulatory harmonization initiatives like ICH (International Council for
Harmonisation) and WHO’s collaborative registration procedures.

Ultimately, regulatory affairs ensure that patients have timely access to safe and effective
medications. It helps companies navigate a highly regulated environment, reduce compliance risks,
and bring innovations to market faster. As the regulatory landscape becomes more complex with the
advent of gene therapy, biosimilars, and personalized medicine, the demand for skilled regulatory
professionals continues to rise. For these reasons, pharma regulatory affairs are not just a support
function—they are a strategic pillar of the pharmaceutical business model.

## 2. Key Global Regulatory Authorities and Their Requirements

Pharmaceutical companies operating globally must adhere to regulatory frameworks set by each
country’s competent authority. These agencies oversee the entire lifecycle of pharmaceutical
products—from clinical trials to marketing authorization and post-market surveillance. The major
regulatory bodies include the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency
(EMA), Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in India, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical
Devices Agency (PMDA) in Japan, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in Australia. Each
agency has its own application formats, timelines, electronic submission systems, and regulatory
expectations, making it crucial for regulatory teams to adopt a tailored approach for each region.

The U.S. FDA regulates drugs, biologics, and medical devices through a robust system that includes
pre-IND (Investigational New Drug) meetings, submission of IND applications for clinical trials, and
final approval via NDA (New Drug Application) or BLA (Biologics License Application). The FDA
mandates submission in electronic format via the Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) using the eCTD
standard. Additionally, periodic safety reporting, annual updates, and compliance with labeling and
promotional guidelines are essential post-approval obligations.

The EMA functions under the centralized procedure, where a single application leads to marketing
authorization across all EU member states. It also supports decentralized and mutual recognition
procedures (DCP and MRP) for drugs not eligible for centralized review. EMA requires rigorous
compliance with ICH guidelines and regional documentation in Module 1 of the eCTD. Scientific
advice, orphan designation, and accelerated assessment pathways are additional features companies
can leverage to expedite approvals.

In India, CDSCO governs drug approvals under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. All
applications—whether for clinical trial permission or marketing authorization—must be submitted
through the SUGAM portal. CDSCO places a strong emphasis on local clinical trial data, especially
for new chemical entities (NCEs). Regulatory submissions must include complete CTD modules, and
products are subject to labeling regulations and import license requirements for foreign
manufacturers. CDSCO also monitors pharmacovigilance through PvPI (Pharmacovigilance Programme of
India).

Other notable agencies include Health Canada, ANVISA (Brazil), SFDA (Saudi Arabia), and Swissmedic
(Switzerland). Some countries, like those in ASEAN, follow the ACTD (ASEAN Common Technical Dossier)
format. To manage this global diversity, many companies develop a core dossier strategy that adapts
to country-specific variations. Regulatory intelligence tools and agency guidance documents play a
critical role in maintaining compliance. Successful navigation of these agencies not only
accelerates product launches but also minimizes the risk of rejections or regulatory penalties.

## 3. The Drug Approval Process: From Development to Market Authorization

The journey of a pharmaceutical product from the laboratory to the patient’s hands involves a
multi-phase regulatory approval process. This process ensures that only safe, effective, and
high-quality drugs are made available to the public. While the specifics may vary across regulatory
jurisdictions, the fundamental framework remains largely consistent worldwide. It comprises
preclinical research, clinical trials (Phases I–III), regulatory submission, marketing
authorization, and post-market surveillance. Regulatory affairs professionals are involved at every
stage, ensuring that the data generated meet regional regulatory standards and that submissions are
complete and accurate.

The first phase, preclinical research, involves in-vitro and animal studies to establish the safety
profile of the investigational compound. Regulatory agencies require this data to approve an
Investigational New Drug (IND) application or its equivalent, which grants permission to begin human
trials. This is followed by clinical trials, which are conducted in three main phases. Phase I
assesses safety and dosage in healthy volunteers. Phase II evaluates efficacy and side effects in a
limited patient population. Phase III confirms effectiveness and monitors adverse reactions in a
larger, diverse group. Regulatory bodies may also require Phase IV or post-marketing studies to
assess long-term effects after a product is launched.

Once clinical data confirms the product’s safety and efficacy, a New Drug Application (NDA) or
Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) is submitted to the appropriate authority. These
submissions must follow specific formats—typically CTD or eCTD—and include extensive data sets
covering quality, non-clinical, and clinical components. Regulatory agencies review these
applications meticulously and may raise questions or request additional data before granting
approval. During this phase, the regulatory affairs team is responsible for managing communication
with the authority, organizing response strategies, and maintaining consistency across submitted
modules.

Approval does not signify the end of regulatory obligations. Post-approval, companies must manage
product labeling, pharmacovigilance reporting, and any lifecycle changes such as new indications,
formulation tweaks, or manufacturing site updates. Variations are classified differently depending
on the region—Type I/II in the EU or PAS/CBE in the U.S. Failure to manage these updates properly
can lead to compliance issues, warning letters, or license suspension. Hence, understanding the full
arc of the drug approval process is essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for a
successful product lifecycle strategy.

## 4. CTD and eCTD: Structure, Importance, and Global Adoption

The Common Technical Document (CTD) is an internationally recognized format for submitting
regulatory information to health authorities. Developed by the International Council for
Harmonisation (ICH), the CTD standardizes the way data is presented in drug applications, thereby
streamlining the review process for regulatory agencies and simplifying dossier preparation for
pharmaceutical companies. The CTD is organized into five modules, each with specific content
requirements. These include administrative and regional information (Module 1), summaries and
overviews (Module 2), quality-related documents (Module 3), nonclinical study reports (Module 4),
and clinical study reports (Module 5).

Module 1 is region-specific and includes forms, cover letters, labeling, and local administrative
documents. Module 2 serves as a bridge between detailed technical data and the reviewers,
summarizing the quality, nonclinical, and clinical information presented in Modules 3–5. Module 3,

# Mastering Global Regulatory Affairs in the Pharmaceutical Industry

## 1. Understanding the Role of Pharma Regulatory Affairs

Pharmaceutical Regulatory Affairs is a multidisciplinary function within the pharmaceutical and
biotechnology industries. It plays a critical role in ensuring that all products—drugs, biologics,
and medical devices—comply with the regulations and standards required by regulatory agencies across
various countries. The regulatory affairs department acts as the interface between pharmaceutical
companies and regulatory bodies such as the FDA (United States), EMA (European Union), CDSCO
(India), PMDA (Japan), and TGA (Australia). These agencies are responsible for reviewing and
approving drug applications, overseeing safety reporting, and enforcing post-approval compliance.

At its core, regulatory affairs involves the preparation, compilation, and submission of a wide
range of regulatory documents. These documents include dossiers (CTD/eCTD), product labels, periodic
safety reports, clinical trial applications, and responses to regulatory queries. In addition, the
regulatory team ensures that the company’s products are registered correctly in each market,
labeling is compliant, and pharmacovigilance systems are in place. Regulatory professionals must
stay up to date with evolving legislation and guidance documents, as non-compliance can result in
delayed product approvals, fines, or even market bans.

The scope of regulatory affairs is not limited to product approval. It extends to lifecycle
management, including post-marketing surveillance, renewals, and variations. Companies often rely on
regulatory intelligence to anticipate changes in global legislation and proactively adjust their
strategies. As global markets expand, pharmaceutical companies increasingly need to harmonize their
regulatory strategies across jurisdictions while addressing country-specific requirements. This need
gives rise to regulatory harmonization initiatives like ICH (International Council for
Harmonisation) and WHO’s collaborative registration procedures.

Ultimately, regulatory affairs ensure that patients have timely access to safe and effective
medications. It helps companies navigate a highly regulated environment, reduce compliance risks,
and bring innovations to market faster. As the regulatory landscape becomes more complex with the
advent of gene therapy, biosimilars, and personalized medicine, the demand for skilled regulatory
professionals continues to rise. For these reasons, pharma regulatory affairs are not just a support
function—they are a strategic pillar of the pharmaceutical business model.

## 2. Key Global Regulatory Authorities and Their Requirements

Pharmaceutical companies operating globally must adhere to regulatory frameworks set by each
country’s competent authority. These agencies oversee the entire lifecycle of pharmaceutical
products—from clinical trials to marketing authorization and post-market surveillance. The major
regulatory bodies include the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), European Medicines Agency
(EMA), Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) in India, the Pharmaceuticals and Medical
Devices Agency (PMDA) in Japan, and the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) in Australia. Each
agency has its own application formats, timelines, electronic submission systems, and regulatory
expectations, making it crucial for regulatory teams to adopt a tailored approach for each region.

The U.S. FDA regulates drugs, biologics, and medical devices through a robust system that includes
pre-IND (Investigational New Drug) meetings, submission of IND applications for clinical trials, and
final approval via NDA (New Drug Application) or BLA (Biologics License Application). The FDA
mandates submission in electronic format via the Electronic Submissions Gateway (ESG) using the eCTD
standard. Additionally, periodic safety reporting, annual updates, and compliance with labeling and
promotional guidelines are essential post-approval obligations.

The EMA functions under the centralized procedure, where a single application leads to marketing
authorization across all EU member states. It also supports decentralized and mutual recognition
procedures (DCP and MRP) for drugs not eligible for centralized review. EMA requires rigorous
compliance with ICH guidelines and regional documentation in Module 1 of the eCTD. Scientific
advice, orphan designation, and accelerated assessment pathways are additional features companies
can leverage to expedite approvals.

In India, CDSCO governs drug approvals under the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019. All
applications—whether for clinical trial permission or marketing authorization—must be submitted
through the SUGAM portal. CDSCO places a strong emphasis on local clinical trial data, especially
for new chemical entities (NCEs). Regulatory submissions must include complete CTD modules, and
products are subject to labeling regulations and import license requirements for foreign
manufacturers. CDSCO also monitors pharmacovigilance through PvPI (Pharmacovigilance Programme of
India).

Other notable agencies include Health Canada, ANVISA (Brazil), SFDA (Saudi Arabia), and Swissmedic
(Switzerland). Some countries, like those in ASEAN, follow the ACTD (ASEAN Common Technical Dossier)
format. To manage this global diversity, many companies develop a core dossier strategy that adapts
to country-specific variations. Regulatory intelligence tools and agency guidance documents play a
critical role in maintaining compliance. Successful navigation of these agencies not only
accelerates product launches but also minimizes the risk of rejections or regulatory penalties.

## 3. The Drug Approval Process: From Development to Market Authorization

The journey of a pharmaceutical product from the laboratory to the patient’s hands involves a
multi-phase regulatory approval process. This process ensures that only safe, effective, and
high-quality drugs are made available to the public. While the specifics may vary across regulatory
jurisdictions, the fundamental framework remains largely consistent worldwide. It comprises
preclinical research, clinical trials (Phases I–III), regulatory submission, marketing
authorization, and post-market surveillance. Regulatory affairs professionals are involved at every
stage, ensuring that the data generated meet regional regulatory standards and that submissions are
complete and accurate.

The first phase, preclinical research, involves in-vitro and animal studies to establish the safety
profile of the investigational compound. Regulatory agencies require this data to approve an
Investigational New Drug (IND) application or its equivalent, which grants permission to begin human
trials. This is followed by clinical trials, which are conducted in three main phases. Phase I
assesses safety and dosage in healthy volunteers. Phase II evaluates efficacy and side effects in a
limited patient population. Phase III confirms effectiveness and monitors adverse reactions in a
larger, diverse group. Regulatory bodies may also require Phase IV or post-marketing studies to
assess long-term effects after a product is launched.

Once clinical data confirms the product’s safety and efficacy, a New Drug Application (NDA) or
Marketing Authorization Application (MAA) is submitted to the appropriate authority. These
submissions must follow specific formats—typically CTD or eCTD—and include extensive data sets
covering quality, non-clinical, and clinical components. Regulatory agencies review these
applications meticulously and may raise questions or request additional data before granting
approval. During this phase, the regulatory affairs team is responsible for managing communication
with the authority, organizing response strategies, and maintaining consistency across submitted
modules.

Approval does not signify the end of regulatory obligations. Post-approval, companies must manage
product labeling, pharmacovigilance reporting, and any lifecycle changes such as new indications,
formulation tweaks, or manufacturing site updates. Variations are classified differently depending
on the region—Type I/II in the EU or PAS/CBE in the U.S. Failure to manage these updates properly
can lead to compliance issues, warning letters, or license suspension. Hence, understanding the full
arc of the drug approval process is essential not only for regulatory compliance but also for a
successful product lifecycle strategy.

## 4. CTD and eCTD: Structure, Importance, and Global Adoption

The Common Technical Document (CTD) is an internationally recognized format for submitting
regulatory information to health authorities. Developed by the International Council for
Harmonisation (ICH), the CTD standardizes the way data is presented in drug applications, thereby
streamlining the review process for regulatory agencies and simplifying dossier preparation for
pharmaceutical companies. The CTD is organized into five modules, each with specific content
requirements. These include administrative and regional information (Module 1), summaries and
overviews (Module 2), quality-related documents (Module 3), nonclinical study reports (Module 4),
and clinical study reports (Module 5).

Module 1 is region-specific and includes forms, cover letters, labeling, and local administrative

# Dependable medical supply support for Indian health organizations.

Tribal Innovations is a Native-owned medical-supply distributor helping Indian Health Service
facilities, tribal healthcare programs, and urban Indian health organizations access the products
they need with responsive, relationship-first service.

[Request a quote][8][View product categories][9]

Why Tribal Innovations

## Native ownership, workflow capability, and fulfillment depth — together

Tribal Innovations combines Native-owned positioning with the operational capability and supply
depth to actually deliver — making us a more credible partner for Indian health organizations.

### Native-owned and procurement-aligned

Built to serve Indian Health Service facilities, tribally operated healthcare programs, and urban
Indian health organizations through a Native-owned business model.

### Workflow capability that supports execution

Tribal’s model is designed to help manage invoicing, account coordination, and the practical steps
required to move orders forward.

### Supply depth through a national partner

The company’s operating model combines community alignment with broader fulfillment infrastructure,
helping reduce the gap between access and reliable delivery.

Who We Serve

## Supporting the organizations at the heart of Indian health procurement

### Indian Health Service facilities

Reliable medical-supply support for Indian health operations.

### Tribally operated healthcare programs

Responsive service built for the way tribal healthcare programs work.

### Urban Indian health organizations

Dependable product access through a Native-owned partner.

[Cardinal Health — authorized distributor partner of Tribal Innovations]

Supply Partnership

## Authorized distributor partner of Cardinal Health

A recurring challenge in this market is vendors who win contracts but lack the supply depth to
fulfill reliably. Tribal Innovations addresses this directly: as an authorized Cardinal Health
distributor, customers get access to Cardinal's full product catalog and fulfillment infrastructure
— through a Native-owned partner.

Access to Cardinal Health's full medical-supply catalog

Reliable fulfillment through an established national supply network

Native-owned positioning without sacrificing product depth or reliability

What We Bring

## Built to deliver, not just to win the contract

Indian health procurement rewards vendors who show up reliably over time. Tribal Innovations is
built around the capabilities that make that possible.

Authorized Cardinal Health distributor — access to a broad national catalog, not a thin sourcing
list.

Native-owned positioning aligned with Indian health procurement pathways and preference programs.

Invoicing and billing support designed for Indian health settings, including coordination with
government payment workflows.

Direct, responsive account management — a real relationship, not a ticketing system.

A fulfillment model built for reliability, so the order that gets placed is the order that arrives.

Family Leadership

## Rooted in Jemez Pueblo, built for the long term

Tribal Innovations is led by a family with deep community roots in Jemez Pueblo and a clear
commitment to service, trust, and long-term follow-through.

[Meet the leadership team][10]
[Allen Gachupin]

### Allen Gachupin

President

Allen Gachupin founded Tribal Innovations and serves as President, leading the company with a
philosophy grounded in service, character, and accountability. A proud Jemez Pueblo tribal member
and U.S. Army veteran, he has dedicated his career to community leadership and building lasting
relationships.

[Kai Gachupin]

### Kai Gachupin

CEO

Kai Gachupin serves as CEO of Tribal Innovations, bringing more than two decades of experience
leading Native-owned businesses in energy, distribution, and government contracting. A proud Jemez
Pueblo tribal member, he leads company strategy and customer development with a long-term focus on
service and reliability.

Start the Relationship

## Ready to work together?

Reach out to Tribal Innovations to discuss your procurement environment, supply needs, or the kind

[Einkorn: The Oldest Ancient Grain Rapidly Gaining Attention from Researchers for Superior Gut
Health][24]
Einkorn is the oldest of the "ancient grains," and its rising popularity in recent years has led to
some interesting findings about this ancient grain, and just how healthy it is. Fortunately, recent
research has looked beyond the modern dogma which claims that the "gluten" found in wheat varieties
is toxic to human health, focusing instead on how wheat is grown and processed, since the gluten
from grains has been a part of the diet of humans for many thousands of years and was always
considered healthy. We have published much of this research ourselves in recent years. More recent
studies, many of them done in Turkey where einkorn (known as Siyez in Turkey) is native, and not an
introduced crop (like in the U.S.), have shown that einkorn is unique in producing lactic acid
bacteria and other "probiotics" necessary for gut health. This is accomplished by using traditional
"sourdough" preparations of the flour. In one study done in Turkey, they added einkorn flour to
"Peksimet", a traditional Turkish twice-baked bread valued for its hard, dry texture, long shelf
life, and role as a durable staple food in Turkish and Turkish-Cypriot cuisine. They found that the
einkorn flour resulted in a significant decrease in the glycemic index, which is important for those
suffering from diabetes or high blood sugar due to the consumption of too many carbohydrates.

## Welcome to VacCure Phrma

Hello and welcome to VacCure Pharma! We are delighted to have you here and thank you for considering
us as your partner in the pharmaceutical industry. Our mission is to provide you with high-quality,
cost-effective pharmaceutical products that meet your unique requirements and specifications.
At our company, we believe in putting our customers first and always strive to exceed your
expectations. Our team of experienced professionals is dedicated to providing exceptional service
and support throughout the entire process - from product selection to delivery. We understand that
the pharmaceutical industry is constantly evolving, and we are committed to staying up-to-date with
the latest developments and trends to ensure that we can offer you the most innovative and effective
solutions.
We are proud to be a reliable and trusted partner in the pharma industry, and we look forward to
working with you. Thank you for choosing us as your pharma exporter.

As a leader in digital health publishing for more than 25 years, WebMD strives to maintain the most
comprehensive and reliable source of health and medical information on the internet.

information platform — and we take that responsibility seriously by:

  Charging our content creators to practice **journalistic principles** of excellence and provide
  objective, accurate, and balanced reporting
* 02
  Maintaining **editorial independence ** and transparency into how we protect the integrity of our
  content
